summary:
The name of the bill is the Building (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 13). The main purpose of this bill is to maintain minimum building safety, manage the overall lifecycle of buildings including planning, design, construction, maintenance, safety assessment, and final management, promote traditional and indigenous skills and materials, maintain a sustainable building construction and management system, and establish a disaster-resilient, climate-adaptive, and environmentally sustainable building system (Objectives and Reasons, Page 1). It shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 13).

The Nepal Government shall bear responsibilities to identify sources and arrange availability of construction materials falling under federal jurisdiction, arrange necessary grants and budget for timber farming, local construction materials, and safe construction technologies, develop an integrated system to coordinate among all three levels, and monitor and evaluate the program at the national level (Section 16g, Page 37). The provincial government shall bear responsibilities to identify and ensure availability of sources of construction materials within its jurisdiction requested by local levels, provide necessary financial, technical, and administrative assistance to local levels, encourage timber farming and production of local construction materials, and arrange necessary budget and programs (Section 16f, Page 36-37). The local level shall bear responsibilities to identify the requirement of local and indigenous construction materials for first residential houses, provide materials from its own area where possible, coordinate with other local levels to provide materials if unavailable, inform eligible families about the source, quantity, and availability of materials, and make the process of providing services and materials single-window and hassle-free (Section 16e, Page 36). To bring necessary arrangements into implementation within one year from the date of commencement of this Act, the Nepal Government, provincial governments, and local levels must prepare necessary budgets, human resources, systems, and action plans within their respective jurisdictions (Section 16j, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 37).

Any person, institution, or government body constructing a building must use quality materials according to approved design and maps and standards specified in the building code (Section 10a, Subsection 1, Page 19). Designers must prepare and certify designs based on prevailing law, building code, and risk assessment, and maintain records of design base, assumptions, calculations, and limits as prescribed (Section 10a, Subsection 2, Page 19). Building construction must be carried out under the supervision of the designer or a supervisor of at least equal qualification, and the supervisor must maintain certified records of inspection, testing, direction, deviation, improvement, and construction works (Section 10a, Subsections 3 and 4, Page 19). Building owners must provide necessary access for supervisor appointment, inspection, and supervision, and keep approved designs, as-built maps, and operation and maintenance records safe after completion (Section 10a, Subsection 6, Page 19). Persons or institutions designing or supervising buildings of specified categories or nature must obtain professional liability insurance, and building owners or constructing persons or institutions must obtain construction risk insurance as prescribed (Section 10a, Subsection 9, Page 20). Building owners or operating bodies must perform regular inspection and maintenance to keep structural and non-structural parts and installed safety and service systems in good condition, prepare and implement an annual maintenance plan for buildings of specified categories or use, and submit annual compliance details to the permit-issuing body (Section 13c, Subsections 1, 2, and 5, Page 27-28). Building owners or operating bodies of specified public use, multi-story, or high-risk buildings must prepare and update an emergency management plan and conduct emergency drills at prescribed intervals while maintaining records (Section 13g, Subsections 1 and 3, Page 31). Regarding deadlines, every government body must enter and update details of buildings under its ownership or management into the national building record system within two years of the commencement of this section (Section 11a, Subsection 2, Page 23) and provide details requested by the Ministry within three months (Section 11a, Subsection 4, Page 23). Every local level must implement an electronic building permit system and integrate it with the national building record system within three years of the commencement of this section (Section 11a, Subsection 6, Page 23). Similarly, every local level must approve required environmental study reports and determine construction material source locations within three months of the commencement of this Act (Section 16d, Subsection 6, Page 36).

Before using new construction technologies, materials, or structural systems not clearly provisioned in the building code, their safety, durability, fire resistance, environmental, and health safety must be certified as meeting prescribed standards and submitted to the committee (Section 9a, Subsection 1, Page 18). Before constructing buildings in risky areas, risk assessments covering geological, geotechnical, seismic, flood, landslide, inundation, emergency access, and other potential risks must be conducted by qualified technicians as prescribed (Section 10b, Subsection 1, Page 20).
